sentences.text: This appeal by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act is arising out of the award dated 29.03.2022 passed by MACT, Mandsaur in MACC No.180/2020 seeking reduction of compensation and in the alternative exoneration from its liability.
2. The brief facts of the case are that claimants/respondents no.1 to 4 filed a claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation for the death of Heeralal in a motor accident on 24.08.2020.

It was alleged before the tribunal that on the date of accident Heeralal was going as pillion rider on an unregistered motorcycle and when they reached opposite Maruti showroom Jamuniya Kala,
Neemuch their motorcycle was hit by car no.RJ-27-CG-6081 because of which Heeralal sustained grievous injuries and died during treatment on 31.08.2020.
A report of the incident was lodged at police station Neemuch against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Appellant and respondent no.5 filed their written statement before the tribunal.

The tribunal framed issues and after taking evidence and hearing counsel for both parties allowed the claim petition filed by respondents No.1 to 4 and awarded a compensation of Rs.17,40,150/- along with interest from the date of filing the petition till its realization.
4. Being aggrieved by the said award, the appellant insurance company has filed this appeal on two grounds i.e. (1) the tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased on the higher side and (2) the National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Anita Bai on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159095720/
1

sentences.text: tribunal has committed error of law and fact by completely overlooking the fact that any document like postmortem report, death certificate confirming the death of deceased is not on record and the tribunal has totally relied on the police investigation.
So prayed for setting aside the impugned award and alternatively prayed for reduction of the amount of compensation awarded by the tribunal.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants have supported the impugned award in regard to the finding of the accident and death of the deceased in the motor accident and also filed a cross objection seeking enhancement of compensation.

It is submitted that the tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.6500/- per month, hence prayed for enhancement of compensation by assessing the income of the deceased on the basis of minimum wages applicable to an unskilled labourer at the relevant period.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing counsel for both parties and on perusal of the record it is found that the accident was occurred on 24.08.2020.
According to the FIR the accident was occurred on 24.08.2020 and the information was received by the police on 3 MA-2843-2022 24.08.2020.
According to the MLC report Ex.P/9 same was done on the same date and he was admitted in hospital till the date of his death i.e. on 31.08.2020.
He was discharged from the hospital on 31.08.2020 and on the same day he died.
According to Ex.P/11 doctor gave a report that deceased died due to accident which was occurred on 24.08.2020.

So considering all the documents it is found that from the date of accident till death of deceased he was under treatment and according to Ex.P/12 the discharge ticket from Kanak hospital it is clear that the deceased was admitted in hospital on 25.08.2020 and discharged on 31.08.2020 and on the same date he died.
So it is clearly established that deceased died due to the injuries sustained by him in the motor accident which was occurred on 24.08.2020.

8. Counsel for the appellant has cited a decision of the coordinate bench of this Court passed in MA No.2684/2023 (Rajesh & others vs. Balram & others) dated 30.01.2024 in which the coordinate bench has held that it is not established that the deceased died in the motor accident as the postmortem report was not produced on record.

entities.text: MA No.2684/2023 (Rajesh & others vs. Balram & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But in the present case it is duly established that the accident occurred on 24.08.2020 and till the death of deceased he was admitted in hospital for treatment.
So it is clearly established that the deceased died due to motor accident.
So the decision cited by the counsel for the appellant is no avail to the appellant.
9. In view of the above discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, in the present case the tribunal has rightly held that the deceased died in a motor accident.
So the argument advanced by the counsel for the insurance company in this regard has no substance.
10. Counsel for the insurance company submits that the tribunal has awarded 4 MA-2843-2022 compensation on the higher side.

On the other hand, counsel for the claimants submits that at the time of accident an unskilled labourer used to get Rs.8275/- per month as minimum wages but the tribunal has calculated the income of the deceased as only Rs.6500/- per month which is on the lower side.

It is true that on the date of accident the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Anita Bai on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159095720/
2 labourer as per the guidelines of the govt. was Rs.8275/- per month.
So in the considered opinion of this Court the tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.6500/- per month in the present case which is enhanced to Rs.8275/- per month.
Thus, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is modified as under:
HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.17,72,505 (i.e. Rs.8,275+40% FP=11,585 x 12=1,39,020 - 1/4th PE=1,04,265 x 17 (M)) Loss of consortium -Rs.1,76,000/-
Medical expenses -Rs.1,38,850/

Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.21,20,335/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.17,40,150/-.
Accordingly, the respondents No.1 to 4/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.3,80,205/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

In the result, the appeal filed by the appellant/insurance being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed whereas the cross objection filed by the respondents No.1 to 4/claimants is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.3,80,205/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
